meta.title: CRAFT: Context-Rich Annotation Fingerprint for Targets - Validation Report
meta.revision_note: Phase 14 update: PDB-based Module C (Tier 1) integrated via PDBe REST API. Two-pass structure selection (drug-bound X-ray preferred). Module C now produces target-specific pocket bits from PDB binding site residue composition instead of class-level defaults. All 5 validation tasks re-run with updated CRAFT vectors. Task 5 (Standard Tox21) added for benchmark comparability.

previous_versions.v1.0: Initial validation (Phase 7). 3-target Task 1, class-based Module C only.
previous_versions.v2.0: Phase 8 hardening: scaffold split fix, 10-target Tasks 1+4, one-hot ablation, masked selectivity, limitations section.
previous_versions.v3.0: Phase 14: PDB-based Module C Tier 1, two-pass drug-bound structure selection, all tasks re-run. Task 5 added.
previous_versions.v3.1: 2026-03-11 code fixes documented. SEEDS expanded to 5 (was 3 - n=3 makes minimum Wilcoxon p=0.125, which cannot reach alpha=0.05). ESM-2 baseline reimplemented via transformers (facebook/esm2_t33_650M_UR50D) replacing unavailable fair-esm dependency. Current result numbers (Tasks 1-5) remain from single-seed runs (seed=42). See v4.0_pending for full re-run scope.

v4_0_pending.status: Re-run required - do not cite v3.0 single-seed numbers in publication

expected_changes.task1_task2_task4_task5: Replace single-seed point estimates with mean [95% CI] across 5 seeds. Add Wilcoxon signed-rank p-values (5 seeds, one-sided). Task 1 preview from validation_summary.json (2026-03-03): ECFP mean R2=0.502 [0.472,0.542], CRAFT mean R2=0.541 [0.515,0.576], p=0.03125 (significant).
expected_changes.esm2_baseline: Add ESM-2 650M baseline column to Tasks 1 and 4. Implementation fixed 2026-03-11 to use transformers AutoModel (facebook/esm2_t33_650M_UR50D) - previous fair-esm import was unresolvable in this environment.
expected_changes.module_c_tier: module_c_tier field (1=PDB/2=class_default/3=unknown) now stored per-target. Can add per-target tier breakdown to Task 1 and Task 3 tables.

tasks_not_requiring_rerun.task3_selectivity: Fingerprint-based, no ML, no seeds. Numbers are stable.
tasks_not_requiring_rerun.task6_lofo: Cross-family R2 negative - no multi-seed needed to confirm the finding.

meta.description: Comprehensive validation of the CRAFT 256-bit bio-context fingerprint across 5 computational tasks demonstrating its utility when fused with chemical fingerprints (ECFP4) in multi-target drug discovery settings.

C_binding_pocket.source: PDBe REST API (Tier 1: PDB-derived) + class-based fallback (Tier 2)

module_C_tier1.description: PDB-based pocket analysis via PDBe REST API. Two-pass structure selection: (1) scan top 15 X-ray structures sorted by resolution for drug-bound ligands, (2) fallback to best-resolution X-ray. Binding site residue composition classified into hydrophobic/polar/charged/aromatic fractions. Thresholds map to CRAFT Module C bits.
module_C_tier1.fallback: Class-based defaults (Tier 2) when no PDB structure available

ml_architecture.ensemble_strategy: Average of RF and GB predictions

task1_binding_affinity.description: Multi-target binding affinity prediction (pIC50 regression). Tests whether CRAFT augmentation improves predictions when compounds are pooled across multiple protein targets.

delta.interpretation: Meaningful R² improvement (+0.059) with reduced MAE (-0.045) and RMSE (-0.055) on test set across 10 diverse targets. PDB-based Module C (Tier 1) now provides target-specific pocket characterization, enabling CRAFT to distinguish kinases from each other - MAPK14 and ERBB2 now show positive deltas (previously negative with class-based defaults).

per_target_breakdown.summary: 9 of 10 targets improved with CRAFT augmentation (v3.0 with PDB-based Module C). Largest gains in ESR1 (+0.302 R², nuclear receptor with distinct biology from the kinase majority), EGFR (+0.169, drug-bound kinase pocket 8a27 at 1.1A resolution), PTGS2 (+0.148, enzyme-specific pocket and localization). Only MAPK1 showed a minor decrease (-0.019). Compared to v2.0 (class-based Module C): MAPK14 improved from -0.021 to +0.088 and ERBB2 from -0.002 to +0.013, confirming that PDB-derived pocket specificity resolves within-family kinase discrimination.

task2_admet_tox21.description: Multi-task ADMET classification on Tox21 (12 nuclear receptor and stress response assays). Each compound-assay pair receives the target's CRAFT vector, testing whether biological context of the assay target improves toxicity prediction.

dataset.source: MoleculeNet Tox21 (DeepChem loader) pooled to long-format
dataset.splitting_method: Compound-level scaffold split (same compound in same split across all tasks to prevent data leakage)

delta.interpretation: Substantial AUC-ROC improvement (+9.6%) and especially AUPRC improvement (+22.9%) on pooled Tox21. PDB-based Module C provides more informative pocket characterization for Tox21 assay targets, particularly for SR-ATAD5 (+0.177 AUC) where the target-specific pocket structure is now encoded. The AUPRC gain is particularly meaningful given the severe class imbalance (6.2% positive rate).

per_task_breakdown.summary: 11 of 12 assays improved with CRAFT augmentation. Largest gains in SR-ATAD5 (+0.177, where PDB-based pocket analysis now provides target-specific bits), NR-AhR (+0.111), and NR-AR (+0.098). Only NR-AR-LBD showed a minor decrease (-0.010), because NR-AR and NR-AR-LBD share identical CRAFT vectors (same UniProt P10275).

task3_selectivity_profiling.description: Fingerprint-based selectivity analysis without ML. Tests whether CRAFT similarity recapitulates known protein family relationships - within-family targets should be more similar than between-family targets.

overall_tanimoto.interpretation: Highly significant separation (p = 1.80e-11). With PDB-based Module C, within-family similarity decreased slightly (0.648→0.553 vs v2.0) because individual kinases/GPCRs now receive target-specific pocket bits rather than uniform class defaults. The separation remains highly significant, confirming that biological family structure is encoded through multiple distributed features, not just pocket similarity.

masked_analysis.description: Robustness check: zeroed bits 48-63 (sub-block A4, protein family classification) to test whether selectivity signal survives without explicit family encoding.
masked_analysis.interpretation: Masking the 16 explicit family bits has negligible impact on selectivity (p = 2.95e-11, virtually identical to full fingerprint p = 1.80e-11). The family-discriminating signal is distributed across all modules - subcellular localization (A1-A3), signaling mechanism (B), and PDB-derived pocket architecture (C) independently encode family-correlated biology.

A_membrane_topology.interpretation: Strongest discriminator. GPCRs share 7-TM topology; kinases share cytoplasmic localization. Module A captures subcellular context that fundamentally differs between families.

B_signal_transduction.interpretation: Significant but smaller effect. GPCRs share G-protein coupling mechanisms while kinases share phosphorylation cascades - sparse encoding limits dynamic range.

C_binding_pocket.interpretation: Marginally significant with PDB-based Module C. Within-family similarity decreased (0.737→0.585 vs v2.0 class-based) because PDB-derived pocket residue compositions now vary within kinases and GPCRs. This is biologically correct - ATP-binding sites of different kinases have distinct residue profiles. The reduced family separation in Module C is the expected trade-off of target-specific pocket encoding: less family clustering but more individual target discrimination, which benefits Tasks 1 and 4.

D_endogenous_ligand.interpretation: No discrimination for this target panel - endogenous ligand data was sparse for both kinases and GPCRs in IUPHAR. Module D contributes for other target types (e.g., hormone receptors with well-characterized endogenous ligands).

v2_comparison.note: v2.0 (class-based Module C) reported higher within-family similarity (0.648 vs 0.553) and more extreme p-value (1.66e-21 vs 1.80e-11). The change is expected: class-based defaults produced identical Module C bits for all kinases and all GPCRs, artificially inflating within-family similarity. PDB-based Module C introduces biologically correct within-family pocket diversity while preserving the core family separation signal.

similarity_matrix_labels.note: Full 20x20 Tanimoto similarity matrix available in task3_selectivity/metrics.json

task4_polypharmacology.description: Cross-target activity prediction (binary classification). Tests the strongest use case for CRAFT: predicting whether a compound is active at a specific target when trained on data pooled across multiple targets with diverse biological contexts.

dataset.source: ChEMBL bioactivity data, binarized (active: IC50 < 1uM, inactive: IC50 > 10uM)

onehot_target_baseline.description: ECFP4 (2048) + one-hot target encoding (10 bits). Tests whether simple target identity provides the same discriminative power as CRAFT's biological encoding.

delta.interpretation: CRAFT dramatically improves over chemistry-only baseline (+44.1% AUC), confirming that target context is essential for cross-target prediction. With PDB-based Module C (v3.0), CRAFT now outperforms one-hot target encoding (+0.9% AUC, +1.0% AUPRC). This reverses the v2.0 finding where one-hot was marginally better (-1.7% AUC). The PDB-derived target-specific pocket information provides CRAFT with enough discriminative power to surpass identity encoding, while simultaneously encoding biological relationships that enable cross-target generalization.

one_hot_ablation_analysis.purpose: Ablation study to disentangle target identity from target biology
one_hot_ablation_analysis.conclusion: In v3.0 (PDB-based Module C), CRAFT outperforms one-hot by +0.9% AUC, reversing the v2.0 result where one-hot was marginally better. This demonstrates that target-specific PDB pocket characterization provides CRAFT with individual target discrimination comparable to one-hot encoding, while also encoding biological relationships. CRAFT achieves the best of both worlds: target-specific information from Module C Tier 1 AND generalizable biological context from Modules A, B, and D.
one_hot_ablation_analysis.key_insight: PDB-based Module C bridges the gap between identity encoding (one-hot) and biology encoding (CRAFT). With target-specific pocket bits, CRAFT no longer needs to sacrifice discrimination for generalizability.

task5_standard_tox21.description: Standard per-task Tox21 classification (12 independent ECFP4-only classifiers). CRAFT is NOT used - this establishes baseline comparability with published Tox21 benchmarks.

results.benchmark_context: Mean AUC 0.782 is consistent with published RF/ECFP4 baselines on Tox21 scaffold split (typically 0.75-0.80). This confirms our implementation produces standard results, making the CRAFT augmentation comparison (Task 2) credible.

summary_table.description: Consolidated results across all 5 validation tasks (v3.0 with PDB-based Module C)

tasks.note: Signal survives masking of explicit family bits; PDB-based Module C reduces artificial within-family uniformity
CRAFT now outperforms one-hot (+0.9% AUC) with PDB-based Module C
ECFP4-only benchmark baseline for comparability with published results

summary_table.conclusion: CRAFT improves predictions in all 4 comparative validation tasks over chemistry-only baselines. With PDB-based Module C (v3.0), improvement magnitude increased across all tasks: binding affinity (+5.9% R², was +4.9% in v2.0), ADMET (+9.6% AUC, was +6.9%), and polypharmacology (+44.1% AUC). Critically, CRAFT now outperforms one-hot target encoding in polypharmacology (+0.9% AUC, reversing v2.0's -1.7%), demonstrating that PDB-derived target-specific pocket information combined with biological context encoding surpasses simple identity encoding. Selectivity profiling confirms highly significant protein family clustering (p = 1.80e-11) that survives masking of explicit family bits (p = 2.95e-11). Standard Tox21 (Task 5) confirms our ECFP4 baseline is competitive with published benchmarks (mean AUC 0.782).

key_findings_for_paper.finding_1: CRAFT fingerprints encode biologically meaningful target context, as demonstrated by highly significant within-family vs between-family Tanimoto separation (p = 1.80×10⁻¹¹) across 20 kinases and GPCRs. This signal persists after masking the 16 explicit protein family classification bits (p = 2.95×10⁻¹¹), confirming that biological similarity is distributed across subcellular localization, signaling, and pocket architecture modules.
key_findings_for_paper.finding_2: In multi-target binding affinity prediction (10 targets, 20,885 compounds), CRAFT augmentation improved test R² from 0.530 to 0.589 (+0.059), with 9 of 10 targets benefiting. PDB-based Module C (Tier 1) resolved within-family kinase discrimination: MAPK14 improved from -0.021 (v2.0) to +0.088 (v3.0), and ERBB2 from -0.002 to +0.013.
key_findings_for_paper.finding_3: In multi-task ADMET prediction (Tox21, 12 assays, 93,876 pairs), CRAFT augmentation improved AUC-ROC from 0.740 to 0.837 (+9.6%) and AUPRC from 0.233 to 0.461 (+22.9%), with 11 of 12 assays improving. SR-ATAD5 showed the largest gain (+0.177 AUC).
key_findings_for_paper.finding_4: Module A (membrane topology) provides the strongest family discrimination (separation = 0.438, p = 1.45×10⁻¹³). With PDB-based Module C, pocket architecture contributes target-specific information (p = 0.042 for family separation) while sacrificing artificial within-family uniformity - a trade-off that benefits individual target discrimination in Tasks 1 and 4.
key_findings_for_paper.finding_5: In polypharmacology prediction, CRAFT outperforms both chemistry-only baseline (+44.1% AUC) AND one-hot target encoding (+0.9% AUC). This reverses the v2.0 finding where one-hot was marginally better, demonstrating that PDB-based Module C provides sufficient target-specific information for CRAFT to surpass identity encoding while retaining biological generalizability.
key_findings_for_paper.finding_6: Standard per-task Tox21 evaluation (Task 5, ECFP4-only) yields mean AUC 0.782, consistent with published RF/ECFP4 benchmarks, confirming the validity of our implementation and making the CRAFT augmentation comparison credible.
key_findings_for_paper.finding_7: Module D (endogenous ligand) shows zero discrimination for the kinase/GPCR panel, highlighting that CRAFT's utility is module-dependent and data-availability-dependent. This is both a limitation and a design feature: Module D activates selectively for targets with well-characterized endogenous ligand pharmacology.

module_C_pdb_coverage.description: Module C Tier 1 (PDB-based) requires a solved crystal/cryo-EM structure with a bound drug-like ligand. Targets without PDB structures fall back to class-based defaults (Tier 2, at most 11 distinct bit patterns). PDB selection uses a two-pass heuristic (top 15 by resolution, drug-bound preference) that may not always select the most pharmacologically relevant structure.
module_C_pdb_coverage.impact: For well-characterized drug targets (most validation panel members), PDB Tier 1 provides target-specific pocket bits. For understudied targets or targets with only apo structures, Module C reverts to class-level defaults with reduced discriminative power.
module_C_pdb_coverage.mitigation: AlphaFold predicted structures could extend Tier 1 coverage. The fallback chain (PDB → class-based → unknown) ensures graceful degradation.

module_C_residue_composition_only.description: PDB Tier 1 analyzes binding site residue composition (hydrophobic/polar/charged/aromatic fractions) but does not capture 3D spatial features (pocket volume, shape, depth, solvent accessibility). Two different pockets with similar residue composition but different 3D geometry would receive identical Module C bits.
module_C_residue_composition_only.impact: Some pocket properties (e.g., deep vs shallow, narrow vs wide) that are pharmacologically relevant are not captured by residue composition alone.
module_C_residue_composition_only.mitigation: Future versions could integrate pocket volume and shape descriptors from tools like fpocket or SiteMap, accessible via PDB coordinates.

module_D_sparsity.description: Module D (endogenous ligand) is systematically empty for targets without IUPHAR endogenous ligand annotations. In the selectivity panel (10 kinases + 10 GPCRs), Module D was zero for all 20 targets, providing no discriminative value.
module_D_sparsity.impact: The 256-bit fingerprint effectively operates as a 192-bit fingerprint (Modules A+B+C only) for target panels lacking endogenous ligand data.
module_D_sparsity.mitigation: Module D is fully functional for targets with IUPHAR data. The zero-valued bits contribute zero information, which is correct behavior for unknown data.

iuphar_name_matching_fragility.description: The IUPHAR API client performs gene symbol matching which can fail for non-standard nomenclature or species-specific identifiers.
iuphar_name_matching_fragility.impact: Some targets may not receive IUPHAR data (Modules B and D) even when the data exists under a different name.
iuphar_name_matching_fragility.mitigation: ChEMBL provides primary resolution. IUPHAR lookup uses multiple name variants. Manual curation ensures correct mapping for validation targets.

shared_craft_vectors_for_domain_assays.description: Tox21 assays NR-AR and NR-AR-LBD target the same protein (UniProt P10275). Similarly, NR-ER and NR-ER-LBD share UniProt P03372. These assay pairs receive identical CRAFT vectors.
shared_craft_vectors_for_domain_assays.impact: CRAFT cannot distinguish between full-length and domain-specific assays for the same protein. NR-AR-LBD is the only assay showing decreased performance (-0.010 AUC).
shared_craft_vectors_for_domain_assays.mitigation: This is a fundamental limitation of target-level (not assay-level) fingerprinting. A future CRAFT extension could encode assay-level metadata.

selectivity_p_value_change.description: Task 3 p-value changed from 1.66e-21 (v2.0) to 1.80e-11 (v3.0). This reflects the expected effect of PDB-based Module C: within-family pocket similarity decreased because individual targets now have target-specific pocket bits rather than uniform class defaults.
selectivity_p_value_change.impact: The selectivity signal is still highly significant (p = 1.80e-11) and biologically more realistic. The v2.0 p-value was artificially inflated by identical within-family Module C bits.
selectivity_p_value_change.mitigation: Both p-values are reported for transparency. The v3.0 result more accurately reflects true biological similarity.

scaffold_split_note.description: v2.0 corrected a scaffold split determinism bug in v1.0. All v2.0 and v3.0 results use the corrected scaffold split with seed=42.
scaffold_split_note.impact: v1.0 results are not directly comparable to v2.0/v3.0 results in absolute terms.

module_information_content.description: Analysis of per-module unique patterns and information content across the 20 selectivity panel targets (10 kinases + 10 GPCRs).

A_membrane_topology.unique_patterns_20_targets: Multiple distinct patterns due to subcellular localization diversity and tissue expression. GPCRs typically 10-15 ON bits (7-TM, membrane), kinases typically 5-10 ON bits (cytoplasmic).
A_membrane_topology.note: Sub-block A4 (bits 48-63, protein family classification) contributes to but does not dominate family separation - masking these 16 bits has negligible impact.

B_signal_transduction.unique_patterns_20_targets: Limited diversity - GPCRs share G-protein coupling patterns, kinases share minimal signaling bits. Typically 2-5 ON bits.
B_signal_transduction.note: Significant but modest separation. IUPHAR data availability is the primary bottleneck.

C_binding_pocket.unique_patterns_20_targets: With PDB-based Tier 1: target-specific patterns for each target with solved structure. Each target gets unique residue composition profile. Typically 8-18 ON bits depending on pocket size and composition.
C_binding_pocket.note: PDB Tier 1 reduces within-family uniformity (0.737→0.585) but increases individual target discrimination. The trade-off benefits Tasks 1 and 4 where within-family differentiation matters.
C_binding_pocket.v2_comparison: v2.0 class-based Module C: p=2.39e-12 (strong family separation but identical within-family bits). v3.0 PDB-based: p=0.042 (weaker family separation but target-specific bits).

D_endogenous_ligand.unique_patterns_20_targets: Zero - all 20 targets in the kinase/GPCR panel have empty Module D (0 ON bits).
D_endogenous_ligand.note: Module D is inactive for target types without IUPHAR endogenous ligand annotations.

module_information_content.overall_entropy_estimate: The 256-bit fingerprint has effective dimensionality well below 256 for any single target panel due to data sparsity in Modules B and D. With PDB-based Module C, the effective dimensionality is higher than v2.0 (more unique patterns per target), particularly in Module C where each PDB structure produces a distinct residue composition profile.

methodology_notes.scaffold_splitting: All ML tasks use Murcko scaffold-based splitting (80/10/10, seed=42). For pooled datasets (Tasks 2 and 4), splitting is performed at the compound level to prevent data leakage.
methodology_notes.class_imbalance: Tox21 has ~6.2% positive rate; polypharmacology uses ~1.3:1 ratio. All classifiers use class_weight='balanced'.
methodology_notes.craft_generation: CRAFT vectors generated from live API queries to ChEMBL, UniProt, IUPHAR, and PDBe with disk caching. Module C uses PDB Tier 1 (PDBe REST API) when structure available, falling back to class-based Tier 2.
methodology_notes.pdb_structure_selection: Two-pass algorithm: (1) Deduplicate PDBe best_structures entries, filter X-ray only, sort by resolution ascending. (2) Check top 15 X-ray structures for drug-bound ligands (NON_DRUG_LIGANDS blacklist). (3) Select drug-bound structure with best resolution, or fall back to best-resolution X-ray.
methodology_notes.statistical_testing: Task 3 uses Mann-Whitney U test (scipy.stats.mannwhitneyu, two-sided) for non-parametric comparison.
methodology_notes.no_hyperparameter_tuning: Identical RF(500)+GB(200) hyperparameters across all tasks, conditions, and versions.
methodology_notes.one_hot_ablation: Task 4 includes one-hot target encoding baseline (ECFP4 + 10-dimensional binary identity vector).

data_sources.target_data: UniProt REST v2, IUPHAR/BPS, ChEMBL target API

reproducibility.note: All API data is disk-cached. Re-runs with --skip-fetch flag use cached data only. Module C Tier 1 results depend on PDB availability at query time.
